issues.legal_issue: An implied agreement to continue a partnership or conduct business in partnership cannot be inferred without adequate support in the evidence.
material_facts: The parties had entered into written partnership agreements for operating a mill business, but the claimed express agreement to continue the partnership after termination of the lease was not proved.

The later documents contemplated the respondent acquiring the mills and potentially forming a company to own and operate them, while giving an appellant only a limited option to acquire company shares.
An appellant had also disclaimed responsibility for business liabilities in correspondence, and the record did not establish an agreement to operate the acquired mills in partnership.
issues.conclusion: No implied agreement to continue the partnership or to operate the mills in partnership could be inferred from the material on record.
issues.legal_principle: An implied agreement must be established by the evidence and cannot be inferred where the parties’ documents and conduct do not support the alleged arrangement. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: partnership_dispute and alleged_implied_continuation and (not express_continuation_agreement_proved) and record_shows_separate_arrangements

predicates.partnership_dispute: The parties disputed whether their business relationship continued as a partnership.
predicates.alleged_implied_continuation: A party relied on the other parties’ conduct and documents to assert an implied agreement to continue the partnership.
predicates.express_continuation_agreement_proved: The parties established an express agreement to continue the partnership.
predicates.record_shows_separate_arrangements: The parties’ documents or conduct showed separate acquisition, ownership, or company arrangements rather than the asserted partnership arrangement.

issues.definition: When a partnership dispute concerns an alleged implied continuation, no express continuation agreement is proved, and the record shows separate arrangements, the rule means that no implied continuation agreement is inferred.

issues.legal_issue: A partnership constituted for a fixed term is dissolved when that term expires unless the partners prove a contrary agreement, and an accounts suit brought outside the applicable limitation period is barred.
material_facts: The partnership agreements fixed the partnership period by reference to the five-year lease term.
The lease possession began on August 31, 1952, and the partnership term therefore expired on August 30, 1957 at the latest.
No agreement to keep the firm in existence after the fixed term was proved.

The suit seeking rendition of accounts was brought on December 20, 1960, more than three years after the fixed term expired; the parties did not dispute that the limitation period for such a suit was three years from dissolution.
issues.conclusion: The firm was dissolved no later than the expiry of its fixed term, and the suit for rendition of accounts was barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 42 of the Indian Partnership Act, subject to a contract between the partners, a firm constituted for a fixed term is dissolved by expiry of that term. The Court distinguished Sathappa Chetty v. S. N. Subrahmanyan Chetty, AIR 1927 PC 70, because it did not concern a firm constituted for a fixed term. The Court applied the undisputed rule that a suit for rendition of accounts must be brought within three years from dissolution.

rule.if: partnership_accounts_limitation_dispute and fixed_term_partnership and (not contrary_extension_agreement_proved) and accounts_suit_brought_more_than_three_years_after_term_end

predicates.partnership_accounts_limitation_dispute: The proceeding concerned a claim for rendition of accounts of a partnership.
predicates.fixed_term_partnership: The partners agreed that the partnership would exist for a fixed term.
predicates.contrary_extension_agreement_proved: The partners proved an agreement to keep the partnership in existence after the fixed term.
predicates.accounts_suit_brought_more_than_three_ye: The accounts suit was filed more than three years after the fixed partnership term expired.

issues.definition: For a partnership accounts claim, where the partnership had a fixed term, no extension agreement is proved, and the suit was brought more than three years after the term ended, the rule means that the accounts claim is time-barred.

issues.legal_issue: After dissolution, partners retain authority and mutual rights and obligations only as necessary to wind up the firm’s affairs and complete transactions begun but unfinished, and action to settle such a transaction does not establish that the firm continued in business.
material_facts: The arbitration concerning the firm’s liabilities to the lessor began while the firm was in existence and remained unresolved when the fixed partnership term expired.
After the term expired, the respondent consented to an award settling that dispute on behalf of the firm.
The consent was given to bring the pending arbitration and the related dispute to an end.
issues.conclusion: The firm’s authority and the partners’ mutual rights and obligations continued only for winding up its affairs and completing pending transactions; the consent to the award did not show that the firm remained in existence after its fixed term.
issues.legal_principle: Section 47 of the Indian Partnership Act continues a partner’s authority to bind the firm, and the partners’ mutual rights and obligations, after dissolution only so far as necessary to wind up the firm’s affairs and complete transactions begun but unfinished, and not otherwise. A transaction includes matters relating to partnership affairs and steps needed to adjudicate a pending dispute. The Court also relied on Lindley on Partnership and Halsbury’s Laws of England for the principle that a dissolved partnership subsists only for completing pending transactions, winding up business, and adjusting partners’ rights.

predicates.dissolved_partnership_dispute: The proceeding concerned the rights or obligations of partners after their firm had been dissolved.
predicates.pending_arbitration_began_before_dissolu: An arbitration concerning the firm began before the firm was dissolved and remained unfinished at dissolution.
predicates.post_dissolution_conduct_settled_pending: After dissolution, a partner acted for the firm to settle the pending arbitration.

issues.definition: Where an arbitration concerning a dissolved partnership began before dissolution and a partner later acted to settle it, the rule means that post-dissolution authority is limited to winding up and settlement, and that act does not establish the firm’s continuation.
